## Why the same order clears once and is stopped the next time

The Korea Customs Service "Customs Clearance Procedures for Overseas Purchases" page states the governing principle plainly: **"Procedures for customs clearance of electronic commerce goods are decided by transportation means."** Courier, post and luggage are three separate regimes with three different sets of numbers. Your assumption that one number covers everything is wrong.

### The three channels, as the KCS pages define them

**1. Express cargo / courier** (*Clearance procedures for express cargo*)
- **List Import Declaration:** personal-use goods **not exceeding USD 150 — "200 dollars for the goods from US"**
- **Simplified Import Declaration:** **USD 150 (200 for US goods) to USD 2,000**
- **General Import Declaration:** **over USD 2,000**, plus anything excluded from the lighter routes
- Duty exemption: total customs value **including shipping cost** must be ≤ USD 150. Above that, **duty and VAT are charged on the whole value, not just the excess**. Tobacco and individual consumption tax are charged even within the exemption.
- 100% X-ray inspection applies to all express cargo.

**2. Post** (*Clearance procedures for postal items*)
- **On-site tax exemption: up to USD 150**
- **On-site taxation / simplified clearance: up to USD 1,000**
- **Import declaration required: over USD 1,000** — half the courier ceiling
- General declaration is also forced for goods for sale, restricted/prohibited goods, and **gifts with dutiable value over 5 million won**.

**3. Your own luggage** (*Customs Clearance Guide for Passengers*)
- **US$800** tax exemption on total taxable value — more than five times the parcel figure
- Separate additional allowances: alcohol up to 2L and US$400, 200 cigarettes, 100ml perfume; no alcohol/tobacco allowance under 19
- Voluntary declaration of excess earns a **30% reduction** in duty; non-declaration detected attracts **40% additional tax, 60% if caught twice within 2 years**.

### The country-dependent rule you asked about
Only one appears: the courier de-minimis is **USD 150 generally but USD 200 for goods from the US**. Note this carefully — the express cargo page attaches the $200 figure to the *List Declaration* rule, while its own *Duty Exemption* paragraph repeats only USD 150. **The postal pages never mention the $200 US figure at all.** So do not assume the US uplift travels with your parcel if you ship by post.

### The likely real cause of your inconsistency
Value may not be the issue. The express cargo page lists goods **excluded from List Declaration regardless of price**, including **health supplements, foods, alcohol and tobacco, certain cosmetics (containing placenta or steroids, or with unidentified elements), quarantine goods (agricultural, fishery, livestock), medicines, wild animal products, and IP-infringing goods**. It also excludes goods where the **description, specification, quantity or price is inaccurately stated** on the clearance list, and goods where new information was added to the waybill. An identical order can therefore be bumped to a formal declaration purely because of the commodity type or a sloppier invoice from the seller.

### Your identifier
The *Issuance of personal customs clearance code* page is explicit: **"When foreigners import E-commerce goods, 'Personal Customs Clearance Code' must be entered ('Foreign Registration Number' and 'Passport Number' are not allowed)."** Your information is correct — a passport number will not work. The code exists so your resident registration number is not exposed. There is an application site linked from that page; per your instruction I did not register anything.

### Ranking for a single order
1. **Luggage** — US$800, by far the most generous, and the only channel with a formal 30% discount for voluntarily declaring an overage. Only viable if you are travelling anyway.
2. **Courier** — USD 150 duty-free (USD 200 from the US), and simplified handling all the way to **USD 2,000**.
3. **Post** — same USD 150 exemption but the formal-declaration cliff arrives at **USD 1,000**, half the courier figure.

**Use courier** for a routine single order you cannot hand-carry. Below USD 150 the outcome is the same as post, but between USD 1,000 and 2,000 courier keeps you in simplified clearance where post would not, and from the US you get an extra $50 of headroom.

### What the pages do not tell you
I am flagging these rather than filling them in: the pages give **no rule on splitting one order into several parcels, or on consolidating multiple parcels arriving the same day** — a common cause of unexpected assessment, but not addressed. They also do not state the **duty and VAT rates** applied above the thresholds, do not give **processing time or validity** for the clearance code, do not confirm whether the **USD 150 exemption is per parcel or per day**, and do not list any **country other than the US** as having a different limit. Nothing on these pages explains whether FTA preference is applied automatically.
